readme: DOES THIS STORE STOCK THIS ITEM AT ALL? One row per (commodity, store) where the answer is no. This is NOT coverage-gap-allowlist.json, which records the opposite case - the store DOES carry it but it cannot be priced like-for-like (unit mismatch, no count in the capture, wrong-product collision). Keeping them apart matters: an unpriceable item is a measurement problem we own, a not-carried item is a fact about the store, and merging them would let the first hide inside the second.
why_this_exists: Measured 2026-08-21: the board holds 3,020 of a possible 3,766 store cells (80.2%). Of the 746 missing, 108 were allowlisted as unpriceable and 638 had no explanation at all - so nobody could tell an item Aldi has never stocked from an item that silently vanished from a store that sells it. audit-coverage-gaps exists precisely to catch the second, and 638 unexplained rows is where that signal goes to die.
basis_field: EVERY entry states how it is known, and the two are never allowed to look alike. 'derived' means the store's own capture recorded the search and what came back - the machine observed it. 'declared' means a human asserted it. A declared entry is worth having and is not worth trusting as far as an observation; the audit reports the split so the ratio is always visible.
expiry: Entries EXPIRE. A store not stocking an item today says nothing about next quarter, and a permanent marker would hide the exact event the gap detector was built to catch - a store beginning, or ceasing, to sell something. recheck_days follows capture-policy.ps1's QuarterDays (90), the same clock the rotation already runs on. Past that an entry is UNVERIFIED, not false: it stops explaining the gap and starts asking to be re-observed.
how_to_grow_the_derived_share: Today only Baker's records per-term capture outcomes keyed by commodity id, so only Baker's rows can be derived. Family Fare records terms but under the budget rotation almost every outcome is not_attempted; Hy-Vee records product ids rather than commodity terms; Aldi, Walmart, Sam's Club and Fareway record nothing at all. The unlock is capture-side, not list-side: have each puller write {term_key, outcome, row_count} the way bakers-regular already does, and this file maintains itself for every store instead of accumulating hand-written assertions.
